newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania party says rulers backed by pyramid firms.
newsitem.headline: Albania party says rulers backed by pyramid firms.

text.p: An Albanian opposition party on Thursday repeated accusations that firms running get-rich-quick schemes in Europe's poorest country had given financial backing to the ruling Democratic Party.

Brushing aside denials and charges of "vile slander" by the conservative Democrats earlier this week, the opposition Democratic Alliance Party (DAP) said the Democrats and the so-called pyramid schemes were two sides of the same coin.
"During the Democratic Party's four years in power the main loan-taking enterprises have systematically served as its financial and psychological support," the DAP said in a statement.

"There are many arguments proving in a direct or indirect way that the ruling party and the firms are two sides of the same coin, cheating Albania's hopes of healthy political and economic development," it added.

The alleged pyramid schemes, some offering 200 percent in three months, have drawn millions of dollars from depositors in Albania over the past few years, taking money away from the banks and alarming world finance organisations.
One of the schemes run by businessman Aleksander Grunasi has collapsed owing $13 million to depositors and two others have temporarily suspended payments to depositors.
President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party on Tuesday rejected earlier DAP charges that it had used money from pyramid schemes to finance its political campaign ahead of a general election last May.
"It is a vile slander characteristic of the Democratic Alliance Party that these firms financed the campaign of the Democratic Party," Democrats spokesman Arben Cejku said.
Cejku said his party had backed the establishment of a special committee to investigate the activity of pyramid schemes.

The DAP also claimed that the Democratic Party's campaign for local elections last October had also been mostly financed by the same firms, and that in one town the symbols of two such companies appeared side by side with the symbol used by the Democrats.
